name: KMVN Tourist Rest House, Binsar
summary: The government rest house inside Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, run by Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam, sits high on the ridge close to the Zero Point trail. Rooms are simple and power is limited, but no other budget stay puts you this close to Binsar's sunrise.
body: KMVN, the Kumaon state tourism corporation, runs a chain of tourist rest houses across the hills, and the Binsar property is one of its best placed. It lies inside the sanctuary near the top of the ridge, about 12 km from the gate on the Almora–Bageshwar road, and a 2 km walk from the watchtower at Zero Point. Around it is mature oak and rhododendron forest.

Expect a government rest house: plain rooms, a dining hall serving simple Indian meals, and staff who know the forest. Electricity inside the sanctuary is limited, so lighting and hot water may run only at certain hours; carry a torch and power bank. Book through the official KMVN website or office, pay the sanctuary gate fee separately, and arrive before dark.
why: Inside the sanctuary, a short walk from Zero Point
Government prices for one of Kumaon's best locations
Forest silence, stars and birds at the door

faqs.q: How do I book the KMVN rest house at Binsar?
faqs.a: Book through the official KMVN website or a KMVN office. Rooms fill on long weekends and in October, so book early. The sanctuary entry fee is paid separately at the gate.

faqs.q: Is there electricity at KMVN Binsar?
faqs.a: Power inside Binsar is limited. The rest house may use solar power and run a generator for a few hours in the evening. Carry a torch and power bank.

faqs.q: Does KMVN Binsar serve food?
faqs.a: Yes, the rest house has a dining hall serving simple Indian meals. There are no shops inside the sanctuary, so bring snacks and any special food you need.

name: KMVN Tourist Rest House, Kausani
summary: Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam's rest house on the Kausani ridge is one of the cheapest ways to wake up facing Trishul and Nanda Devi. It is plain and government-run, but its position on the ridge is what Kausani is about.
body: The rest house sits on the ridge in Kausani with a wide view of the peaks to the north, often mentioned as one of the best viewpoints in the village. It is a short walk from the bus stand, the Anasakti Ashram and the Pant museum, which makes it easy for travellers arriving by shared jeep or bus.

Rooms are basic, with simple furnishings and heating that varies; ask for a room facing the mountains. The kitchen serves Indian meals. Like all KMVN properties, bookings are made through the official KMVN website or offices, and service is straightforward rather than polished. For saver trips it offers excellent value, especially from October to February.
why: Ridge-top position with a full Himalaya view
Walking distance from the bus stand and Anasakti Ashram
Government prices

faqs.q: Does KMVN Kausani have mountain views?
faqs.a: Yes, the rest house stands on the ridge facing the Trishul and Nanda Devi groups. Ask for a north-facing room when you book.

faqs.q: How far is KMVN Kausani from the bus stand?
faqs.a: It is a short walk or quick taxi ride from the Kausani bus and jeep stand. Ask the driver to drop you at the KMVN rest house.

faqs.q: Is the KMVN rest house in Kausani heated?
faqs.a: Heating varies by room and season, and may be by electric heater on request. Nights are cold from November to February, so pack warm layers.

name: Zostel Mukteshwar
summary: Zostel's Mukteshwar hostel is a favourite of students, solo travellers and remote workers, with dorm beds and private rooms, a garden with fruit trees, terraces and a café on the ridge outside town.
body: Zostel is one of India's best-known backpacker hostel chains, and its Mukteshwar property sits among orchards outside the town, about 28 km from Bhimtal. It has dormitories and private rooms, shared lounges, terraces facing the valley and an on-site café. The garden has fruit trees such as lemon, apricot and plum.

The crowd is young and social, and many guests stay for a week or more to work remotely. It is a good base for walks to the Mukteshwar temple and Chauli ki Jali, village hikes and the rappelling sessions on the cliffs. Nights are cold from November to February, so check what heating and hot water are available when you book.
why: Dorm beds at saver prices on a quiet ridge
Social space for solo travellers and remote workers
Orchard setting with valley views
price_band: ₹600–1,000 a dorm bed; ₹2,000–4,000 for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Is Zostel Mukteshwar good for remote work?
faqs.a: Many guests work remotely from here. Mobile 4G works in the area and the hostel has common work spaces. Ask about Wi-Fi speed and power backup before booking a long stay.

faqs.q: Does Zostel Mukteshwar have private rooms?
faqs.a: Yes, alongside dormitory beds it offers private rooms for couples and small groups. Prices rise on weekends and holidays.

faqs.q: How do I reach Zostel Mukteshwar?
faqs.a: Take a shared taxi from Kathgodam or Haldwani to Bhowali, then to Mukteshwar, or a private taxi for about ₹2,500–3,500. The hostel can advise on the last stretch.

name: The Naini Retreat
summary: A heritage hotel on the Ayarpata slopes above Naini lake, once a residence of the Maharaja of Pilibhit, run by Leisure Hotels as part of IHCL's SeleQtions collection. It offers lake views, gardens and quiet above the Mall.
body: The Naini Retreat sits at about 1,995 m on the wooded Ayarpata side of Nainital, above the lake and away from the noise of the Mall. The main building was historically a residence of the Maharaja of Pilibhit. The hotel is operated by the Leisure Hotels group and joined Indian Hotels Company's SeleQtions collection, which brings brand standards to an older property.

The grounds cover more than five acres of garden and forest, and many rooms have large bay windows facing the valley or lake. The hotel has dining options, a bar and a spa. It is a short drive or a steep walk to the Mall and the lake, which suits families and couples who want comfort and calm while still seeing Nainital on foot.
why: Lake and valley views from a quiet slope
Heritage building with modern comforts
Gardens and forest within the grounds

faqs.q: Where is The Naini Retreat in Nainital?
faqs.a: It is on the Ayarpata slopes on the southern side of Nainital, above the lake. The Mall and the lake are a short drive or a steep walk away.

faqs.q: Is The Naini Retreat a heritage property?
faqs.a: Yes. The building was historically a residence of the Maharaja of Pilibhit and now runs as a heritage hotel under Leisure Hotels, within IHCL's SeleQtions collection.

faqs.q: Is The Naini Retreat good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. It offers space, gardens and a quieter setting than hotels on the Mall, with dining on site. The slopes mean some steps and walking, so check access if travelling with seniors.

name: West View, Ranikhet
summary: A heritage hotel built in 1918 on a forested plateau above Ranikhet, with timber-framed architecture, high-ceilinged rooms with fireplaces and gardens shaded by deodar and pine. It suits travellers who like old buildings and slow evenings.
body: West View stands on about 5 acres of deodar and pine forest overlooking the western valley of Ranikhet, a short drive from the Mall and Sadar Bazaar. The building dates from 1918 and has been a hotel for decades, with Queen Anne-style details, timber framing and parquet floors that recall Ranikhet's cantonment past.

Rooms have high ceilings and many have fireplaces, which matter on winter nights. The lounge, dining room and garden sit-outs are the hotel's heart. Expect the character and occasional quirks of an old building rather than a modern resort. It is a comfortable base for the regimental museum, Chaubatia and Jhula Devi, and a good stop between Nainital and Kausani.
why: A 1918 building with Raj-era character
Quiet forest grounds close to town
Fireplaces for cold evenings

faqs.q: How old is West View hotel in Ranikhet?
faqs.a: The building dates from 1918 and has long run as a heritage hotel. It keeps much of its original architecture, including timber framing and parquet floors.

faqs.q: Is West View close to Ranikhet town?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a short drive from the Mall and Sadar Bazaar, set on its own forested grounds above the western valley.

faqs.q: Does West View have fireplaces?
faqs.a: Many rooms have fireplaces, which are welcome from November to February. Ask the hotel whether a fire can be lit for your room when you book.

name: The Ramgarh Bungalows
summary: Neemrana's set of restored 19th-century cottages at Ramgarh, about 25 km before Mukteshwar, stands among orchards that supply its own jams. Quiet, old-fashioned and well suited to writers and slow stays.
body: Neemrana Hotels restores old buildings across India, and at Ramgarh it runs a group of colonial-era cottages in Malla Ramgarh, about 35 km from Nainital on the road to Mukteshwar. The Old Bungalow is the oldest building in Ramgarh and was once a dak bungalow, a halt for officials and post on horseback. Other cottages are spread across the slope.

The orchards around the bungalows grow apricots, plums, peaches, pears and apples in summer, and the estate makes jams from them. Meals include Kumaoni dishes and breakfasts outdoors facing the hills. Ramgarh's links with the poet Mahadevi Verma and with Rabindranath Tagore make it a natural base for a writing retreat, and Mukteshwar's temple and cliffs are a short drive away.
why: Restored 19th-century cottages with character
Orchard setting with home-made jams
Quiet base for writers and long stays

faqs.q: Where are the Ramgarh Bungalows?
faqs.a: In Malla Ramgarh on the Bhowali–Mukteshwar road, about 35 km from Nainital and 25 km before Mukteshwar.

faqs.q: What is special about the Ramgarh Bungalows?
faqs.a: They are restored colonial cottages, including an old dak bungalow, set in orchards that produce fruit for the estate's jams. The setting is quiet and suited to long, slow stays.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at Ramgarh?
faqs.a: April for blossom, June to August for fruit, and October to December for clear views. Winters are cold, so check heating when booking.

name: The Kumaon
summary: A small, design-led hotel on a terraced slope at Kasar Devi above Almora, with stone and timber chalets facing the high Himalaya. Its architecture won wide attention and it is one of the best places to stay in Kumaon.
body: The Kumaon was designed by the Sri Lankan practice Zowa Architects for a sloping, terraced site at Kasar Devi, about 8 km from Almora. Rooms are arranged in pairs, one chalet above another, and scattered across the slope to keep the buildings low. The lower chalets use stone quarried nearby; the upper ones have walls clad in bamboo, and terraces are paved in kota stone.

The effect is simple and quiet: large windows on the mountains, unplastered concrete, and terraces among pine and oak. The hotel is a good base for Kasar Devi, Crank's Ridge, Almora's Lal Bazaar, Binsar and Jageshwar. Rates are high and rooms few, so book well ahead for October and November, when the views are clearest.
why: Distinctive architecture rooted in local materials
Direct views of the high Himalaya from Kasar Devi
Small and quiet, close to Almora and Binsar

faqs.q: Where is The Kumaon hotel?
faqs.a: At Kasar Devi, about 8 km from Almora on the Binsar road, on a terraced slope facing the Himalaya.

faqs.q: Who designed The Kumaon?
faqs.a: The hotel was designed by Zowa Architects, a Sri Lankan practice, using local stone, bamboo cladding and terraces that follow the slope.

faqs.q: Is The Kumaon suitable for children?
faqs.a: The site is steep with many steps and the mood is quiet, so it suits couples and adults best. Ask the hotel directly about its policy on young children.

name: Mary Budden Estate
brand: Independent (Small Luxury Hotels of the World)
summary: A restored 19th-century estate inside Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, named after its last known resident, Mary Budden. Run on solar power and harvested rainwater, it offers a handful of rooms, home-style meals and guided forest walks.
body: Mary Budden Estate is one of a few privately owned estates that predate Binsar's 1988 sanctuary status. The heritage cottage, empty for decades, was restored and opened to guests in 2011, with a newer cottage added nearby. The estate covers about five acres of oak and rhododendron forest at around 2,400 m, and is listed with Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

Binsar is walking country, and the estate has mapped walks of different lengths through the sanctuary, with guides who know its birds and plants. It runs on solar power and rainwater harvesting and aims to be plastic-free, so expect limited electricity and no television. Meals are home-style and often Kumaoni. Book well ahead; rooms are few.
why: Heritage estate inside Binsar's oak forest
Guided walks and birding from the door
Solar-powered, plastic-free and very quiet

faqs.q: Is Mary Budden Estate inside Binsar sanctuary?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of a few private estates inside Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary. Guests pay the sanctuary entry fee at the gate.

faqs.q: Is there electricity at Mary Budden Estate?
faqs.a: The estate runs on solar power and rainwater harvesting, so electricity is limited. Expect lights and charging but no heavy appliances or television.

faqs.q: What is there to do at Mary Budden Estate?
faqs.a: Guided forest walks, birding, the Zero Point sunrise, reading and meals by the fire. It suits travellers who want quiet rather than sightseeing.

name: Te Aroha by Shervani, Dhanachuli
summary: A boutique hotel at Dhanachuli near Mukteshwar, with suites and cottages facing the snow peaks and a restaurant with outdoor seating. Now run by Shervani Hotels, it suits couples and families who want comfort with walks and waterfalls nearby.
body: Te Aroha stands in the village of Dhanachuli, on the ridge road near Mukteshwar, about 53 km from Kathgodam. It was built as a boutique hotel with an artist's touch and is now operated by Shervani Hotels as Te Aroha by Shervani. Accommodation ranges from rooms to suites and cottages, many with balconies facing the Himalaya.

The in-house restaurant, Café Flashback, serves Indian and international dishes indoors and outdoors. The hotel arranges forest walks, visits to the Bhalu Gaad waterfall and village outings. It works as a calm signature base for Mukteshwar, Ramgarh and Nainital, about 1.5 hours away. Book early for the New Year week and October.
why: Suites and cottages with snow-peak views
Quiet ridge setting near Mukteshwar
Walks to Bhalu Gaad waterfall and villages

faqs.q: Where is Te Aroha?
faqs.a: In Dhanachuli village near Mukteshwar, about 53 km from Kathgodam and roughly 1.5 hours from Nainital.

faqs.q: Who runs Te Aroha now?
faqs.a: It is operated by Shervani Hotels and marketed as Te Aroha by Shervani, Mukteshwar.

faqs.q: What activities does Te Aroha offer?
faqs.a: Forest walks and treks, visits to the Bhalu Gaad waterfall, village visits and quiet days with mountain views. Ask the hotel for current options when you book.
